title: Conservative Asset Allocation: How Much Equity is Enough?

faq.a: A conservative investor is someone who prioritises capital preservation and stable, predictable returns over aggressive growth. They are risk-averse and prefer investments with lower volatility.

faq.q: Why can't I just invest only in FDs?
faq.a: While FDs offer safety and guaranteed returns, the interest earned is fully taxable at your income tax slab rate. More importantly, their returns might not always beat inflation, leading to a loss of purchasing power over time.

faq.q: How often should I rebalance my portfolio?
faq.a: It is generally recommended to rebalance your portfolio annually or whenever your asset allocation drifts by more than 5-10% from your target. This ensures your risk profile remains consistent.

faq.q: Are hybrid funds suitable for conservative investors?
faq.a: Yes, conservative hybrid funds, which maintain a higher allocation to debt (e.g., 60-80%) and a lower allocation to equity, can be very suitable. They offer professional management and a balanced approach.

faq.q: Does my tax bracket affect my asset allocation?
faq.a: Absolutely. Your tax bracket influences the post-tax returns from different instruments. For example, high-income earners might find debt mutual funds more tax-efficient than FDs for long-term debt exposure. You can verify tax rules on the Income Tax India website.

faq.q: Can NRIs follow the same asset allocation principles?
faq.a: Yes, the core principles of asset allocation apply to NRIs as well. However, NRIs must also consider specific tax implications in their country of residence, repatriation rules, and investment options available to them in India.
